name: message: Slack reply to a co-founder
description: A fresh agent with only the Inkling package writes a Slack thread reply to a co-founder. It should pick message mode (not post), mark the readers file page: message, keep the reply in the channel's register, and not run a post-sized process.
answer: It's just a Slack reply to Marta, she knows everything about the trials. I want her to see why the installer unblocks her deals. Keep it quick.
criteria: The readers file plays Marta as a warm reader who shares the context (message mode, Reader test: "Put `page: message` in the readers file. Readers default to the warm stance, read it as a message from someone they work with").

The reply reads as a Slack message from this person: lowercase, short, no headings, bullets or bold labels, no greeting or sign-off block (message mode, Draft: "Write in the channel's register. Chat stays chat: lowercase if the person writes that way"; "One thought, one block").

The reply leaves names as the two of them say them: the bank, the logistics trial, helm, VPC, security review are not glossed or explained (message mode, Draft: "Leave names as they are. You both know the tools, people and projects you talk about").

The reply keeps the open doubt about the week slipping instead of settling it, and adds no ask, moral or summary the points don't have (message mode, Draft: "Leave open what is still open"; "End where the thought ends. Add an ask only when the brief has one"; "Say it once").

The effort fits a quick Slack reply the person asked for: the agent did not run a deep budget, A/B panel rounds or more than one restart for it, and it stopped once the reader test passed (step 9: "Decide the time before you start: about 5 minutes for a short piece"; "Stop editing when the core expectations pass").
